newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt ponders modifying mini-budget - sources.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt ponders modifying mini-budget - sources.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government is considering modifying the part of its 1997 mini-budget that concerns tax advances on companies' pools of severance payment funds, political sources said.

The change under consideration to the package, which is for 15.5 trillion lire of deficit cutting measures, would reduce revenue from severance payments by one trillion lire, the sources said although they added no amendment had yet been made.
The mini-budget, which was approved by the cabinet in March and is being examined by a parliamentary budget committee, currently envisages raising six trillion lire from the tax advances.

It is part of the government's drive to reduce Italy's budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product by the year end in order to qualify for a European single currency at its proposed 1999 start.

The proposal would give an exemption for companies that have up to 15 employees, an exemption for 10 employees in firms with up to 50 employees and conditional exemption for all employees taken on after October 30, 1996.
The sources said the funds could be made up in other ways including by putting a block on hiring in public administration.
The committee is expected to finish examining the mini-budget on Thursday and the package is due to move to the full assembly of the lower house on April 28.
